Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice E.S.Indiresh
 Oral Judgment

This appeal is arising out of the judgment and award dated 12.12.2018 in MVC No.174/2014 on the file of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-VI, Vijayapur, dismissing the claim petition filed by the claimant.

entities.text: I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-VI, Vijayapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. It is the case of the claimant that, on 22.06.2013, the claimant was proceeding on the edge of the road and at that time, a tractor and trailer bearing Reg. No.KA-28/T-3068 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the claimant and as a result of the same, the claimant sustained severe injuries.
Hence, claimant has filed MVC No.174/2014, seeking compensation from the respondents.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:1024 HC-KAR 3.
Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte Respondent.
No.2 - Insurance Company contested the matter on merits.
4. In order to establish the case, the claimant has examined three witnesses as PWs.1 to 3 and got marked 12 documents as Exs.P1 to P12.

The respondents have examined two witnesses as RWs.1 and 2 and got marked 06 documents as Exs.R1 to R6.
5.

The Tribunal, after considering the material on record, by judgment and award dated 12.12.2018,
dismissed the claim petition.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant has preferred this appeal.

2 6. I have heard Sri Sanganagouda V. Biradar, learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Sri S.S. Aspalli, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2- Insurance Company.
7.

It is submitted by Sri Sanganagouda V. Biradar, learned counsel appearing for the appellant that,
the NC: 2026:KHC-K:1024 HC-KAR alleged accident was occurred on account of the rash and negligent driving of the tractor and therefore, the finding recorded by the Tribunal, dismissing the claim petition is non est and requires to be interfered with in this appeal.

It is also argued by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant that, after the claimant sustaining injuries, he was admitted to Tanga Multi Speciality Hospital and Trauma Centre, Bijapur and thereafter, the complaint was lodged by the father of the claimant as per Ex.P2 to conduct investigation by the police authorities.

Therefore, it is contended by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant that,
the finding recorded by the Tribunal requires to be interfered with in this appeal.

8. Per contra Sri S.S. Aspalli, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2-Insurance Company sought to justify the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and invited the attention of the Court to Ex.P2 and submitted that, the offending vehicle has been wrongly NC: 2026:KHC-K:1024 HC-KAR implicated to claim compensation and therefore, sought for dismissal of the appeal.
9.
In the light of the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, I have carefully examined the finding recorded by the Tribunal.
It is not in dispute that, the alleged accident was occurred on 22.06.2013 and the complaint at Ex.P2 was lodged after five days.

In the said complaint, it is stated as follows:

11. Perusal of the deposition of PW.1 (mother of the claimant) and the complaint averments at Ex.P2 (given by the father of the claimant) runs contrary to each other as to occurrence of the accident is concerned.
It is also to be noted that, there is a delay of five days in lodging the complaint-Ex.P2.

Though PW.2 - doctor deposed that the said hospital has sent MLC report to the Gandhi Chowk Police Station on the date of the accident itself, however, there is no material as to the date on which the MLC report was forwarded to the jurisdictional police.

In that view of the matter, taking into consideration the finding recorded by the Tribunal at paragraph 9 of the impugned NC:
2026:KHC-K:1024 HC-KAR judgment, I am of the view that, no interference is called for in this appeal.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
